claim: A defendant raising an ineffective assistance of counsel claim on direct appeal must make specific allegations of the conduct that constitutes deficient performance only when the alleged deficiency involves the failure to file pretrial motions, but not when the alleged deficiency concerns voir dire conduct.
initial_reasoning: The cited opinion (984 N.W.2d 261) holds that on direct appeal a defendant must allege specific conduct constituting deficient performance for any ineffective‑assistance claim, including both voir dire conduct and failure to file pretrial motions. It does not limit the specificity requirement to pretrial motions alone.
